exposure: skin-to-skin contact (SSC) during the third stage of labour
cohort: Mothers and newborns undergoing skin-to-skin contact during the third stage of labour, as observed across 18 prospective clinical trials.
finding: Skin-to-skin contact during the third stage of labour was associated with a reduction in the incidence of uterine atony, a lower likelihood of blood loss greater than or equal to 500 mL, and a decrease in mean postpartum blood loss, but no significant differences were found in the incidence of severe postpartum haemorrhage.
mod_finding: Further high-quality research is needed to confirm these benefits, particularly in caesarean sections.
